english.notes:
(i) This is the NON-ENDORSABLE VERSION of the offence and should BE USED:-
(a) In circumstances where the offender’s driving would have been in accordance with any licence that could have been granted to him e.g. where the entitlement period to drive the category of vehicle has expired but where the driver would have been granted a licence had they applied OR
(b) where the driver has had his licence to drive revoked because of a failure to surrender it for endorsement, then, provided his / her driving would have been in accordance with that licence this non endorseable offence wording should be used.
(ii) Where the offender held, or could have been granted, a driving licence authorising the driving of the vehicle in question AND he / she was driving in circumstances that were not or would not have been in accordance with that licence - that offence is liable to endorsement and officers should refer to the endorsable version in document H31 (CJS code RT88334).
(iii) Where the offenders licence has been revoked or refused by DVLA for a medical / disability reason, the offence under section 94A of the Road Traffic Act 1988 in document H9153 (CJS code RT88139) should be considered. The penalty for the section 94A offence is endorsable and imprisonable - akin to driving whilst disqualified.
(iv) The item in Schedule 2 to the Road Traffic Offenders Act relating to section 87(1) provides that endorsement and disqualification apply "in a case where the offender's driving would not have been in accordance with any licence that could have been granted to him".
